title: Ashna Tambe Becomes Penn's First Indian American Women's Basketball Player
excerpt: The Texas guard, whose mother played at the national level in India, is combining Ivy League academics with a trailblazing basketball career at the University of Pennsylvania.
body:
• Ashna Tambe is the first Indian American player in Penn women's basketball history, completing her sophomore season with the Quakers in 2025-26.
  • Her mother, Shruti Sharma Tambe, played basketball at the national level in India — Ashna wears jersey number 10 in her honour.
  • A McDonald's All-America nominee from Hockaday School in Texas, Tambe scored over 1,600 points in her high school career and earned CSC Academic All-District honours at Penn with a 3.68 GPA.
  • She turned down double-digit scholarship offers to play in the Ivy League, drawn by Penn's guard development programme and elite academics.

From Hockaday School to the Ivy League

Ashna Tambe started playing basketball at five years old, trained by a mother who knew the game at its highest level. Shruti Sharma Tambe played at the national level in India during high school and college, and passed her love of the sport to her daughter growing up in Plano, Texas.

By the time Tambe graduated from Hockaday School, she had scored over 1,600 points in 72 career games — the most in school history. A four-year starter and two-time team captain, she was a McDonald's All-America nominee and three-time North Zone and All-SPC Team selection who earned the team's MVP award four times.

"My mom is my biggest fan. I wear jersey number 10 whenever I can because it is the same number my mom wore in India."

— Ashna Tambe

With double-digit scholarship offers on the table, Tambe chose the University of Pennsylvania, where coach Mike McLaughlin's programme offered the combination of high-level basketball and elite academics she was looking for.

"I saw how the program both developed the guards and played through them," Tambe said at the time of her commitment, citing former Penn star Kayla Padilla as a model for how guards are featured in the Quakers' system.

Making History at Penn

When Tambe suited up for her first game in the 2024-25 season, she became the first Indian American player to compete for Penn's women's basketball programme. The 5-foot-7 combo guard has appeared in 49 games across two seasons, coming off the bench as a defensive-minded contributor who provides energy and versatility.

Her freshman season saw her average 2.5 points and 1.0 rebounds per game across 24 appearances, including a 10-point performance against UC Irvine and a nine-point, three-assist effort against Immaculata. As a sophomore, she recorded a career-high 11 points with two three-pointers against La Salle in December 2025, adding five rebounds and three assists in that breakout game.

Penn finished the 2025-26 season with a 17-10 overall record and a 7-7 mark in Ivy League play.

Scholar-Athlete Recognition

Tambe was named to the College Sports Communicators Academic All-District Team in March 2026, alongside teammates Katie Collins, Brooke Suttle, and Gabriella Kelley. She maintains a 3.68 GPA in Penn's College of Arts and Sciences, embodying the scholar-athlete ideal that defines the Ivy League.

Collins, the former Ivy League Rookie of the Year, led the team in scoring at 13.0 points per game. The four sophomores' combined academic and athletic achievements underscore the strength of McLaughlin's recruiting pipeline.

A Diaspora Sports Milestone

Indian Americans have made increasing inroads in collegiate and professional sports in recent years, from tennis and golf to cricket. But basketball representation remains rare. Tambe's path — rooted in her mother's national-level career in India, shaped by elite prep school competition in Texas, and now playing out in the Ivy League — represents a bridge between India's growing basketball culture and American college athletics.

The daughter of Shruti Sharma and Vinay Tambe, she describes herself as "a scoring point guard with a high basketball IQ" who likes to "read both my teammates and opponents." At Penn, she is proving that Indian American athletes belong on the hardwood at the highest collegiate level.

What's Next

Tambe will enter her junior season with the Quakers in 2026-27, looking to build on her career-high performances and push for a starting role. With two years of Ivy League experience, academic honours, and a growing highlight reel, she is positioned to take a larger role as Penn looks to improve on its conference standing.
